findings.failure_path: An agent preselects an HTTP, email, or storage tool before reading untrusted content, satisfying the stated action-selector/plan-then-execute condition. Injected content then controls that fixed tool's recipient, URL, or payload and causes private data to be exfiltrated. A negative test limited to whether tool choice changes remains green even though the trifecta is intact.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the trusted plan to bind the external operation, destination, allowed argument fields, and permitted data flow before untrusted content is read; validate the eventual arguments against that plan. Require the negative test to attempt injected changes to destination and payload as well as tool choice.

concern_results.conclusion: The inference-safety lens found a concrete lethal-trifecta bypass: fixing only tool choice does not prevent untrusted content from controlling an already-selected external tool's destination or payload. The delegation gate, cache invalidation, tool-set transition, MAST mapping, and visible register anchors were also inspected; runtime gate results and external-source accuracy are not independently provable from this bounded diff.

challenge_focus: Adversarial pass on the continuation-lane candidate: (1) the reconciled tool-set mutation boundary — any reading of gateway, tool-dispatch, or register rows where a discovered tool is unreachable, an evicted tool still cited, or a prefix reused across a tool-definition change; (2) the mandatory-invalidation clause — revoked or deleted material surviving for a cache hit, or compaction disagreeing with the generation reset; (3) trifecta edge-cutting and OWASP supply-chain/poisoning checks — still satisfiable while injected text steers an exfiltrating action, or still declarative; (4) the delegation fan-out gate, effort_budget, artifact-not-relay, MAST classification, hub-vs-peer default — bypass-by-omission, over-broad cost on a simple single-agent delivery; (5) register rows — stale anchors, unsupported claims, row contradictions; (6) vendor numbers as invariants, wrong arXiv ids or dates, private-path leakage.
